"""Concept: birth, life and generation (the meaning of the Chinese 生, and English words for it).

The unit responds to words about coming into being: birth and being born; life and living;
generating, producing, reproducing; growing, developing, creating; arising, appearing, evolving.
The Chinese character 生 (life, birth, to produce) is its strongest trigger: on its own it is
about 8, and in compounds such as 一生, 人生, 生态, 产生, 发生, 生活, 学生 about 2.4.
Other words get a smaller positive value; everything else is 0.
Tiers, from the mean activation on training text:
  生 alone 8; 生-compounds 2.4; birth/born 1.8; life/generate/produce/reproduce/bio ~1.3;
  create/develop/grow/come/exist/arise-type words, incl. 成/形成/出现/发展, ~0.7.
"""

READS = ()

ZH_ALONE = "生"
BIRTH = {"birth", "births", "born", "birthday"}
LIFE_MAKE = set("""life lives living lived live alive lifetime survival bio biology wildlife
generate generated generates generating generation generations generator
produce produced produces producing production producer
reproduce reproduction reproductive
emerge emerged emerging arise arose arises arising
产 生命 产生 生活 生物
""".split())
GROW_BECOME = set("""create created creates creating creation develop developed developing development
grow grew grown growing growth form formed formation forming
come came comes coming exist exists existence occur occurred occurs happen happened happens happening
appear appeared appears appearance origin origins evolve evolved evolution native
rise rising raise raised introduced introduce early derive derived died
nature natural naturally student students graduate
成 形成 出现 出来 起来 成立 存在 活 发展 发 开发 发育 进化 起源 成长
""".split())


def score(tok):
    word = tok.strip().lower()
    if tok.strip() == ZH_ALONE:
        return 8.0
    if ZH_ALONE in tok:
        return 2.4
    if word in BIRTH:
        return 1.8
    if word in LIFE_MAKE:
        return 1.3
    if word in GROW_BECOME:
        return 0.7
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Stateless: looks only at the newest token."""
    return None, score(prefix.token_strings[-1])

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:1539 - a "France / French" token detector, with small
function-word effects.

The component's activation is set mostly by the current token, not by the words before it.
Its largest negative values are on tokens that name France, French, or French places and
cities (France, French, Paris, Québec, Marseille, Belgium, Saint, ville, ...). Tokens
written with French accents (é, è, à, ç, ô, ...) are mildly negative. Two common words
add a small shift: " de" and " et" are slightly negative, and " pour" and " à" are
positive inside French text. Everything else sits near zero, so the program predicts 0.
"""

import re

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Names of France, French, and French-speaking places, plus French name fragments.
FRENCH_PLACE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(france|french|fran[cç]ais\w*|paris|qu[ée]bec|montr[ée]al|marseille|lyon|"
    r"bordeaux|montpellier|strasbourg|belgi\w*|lorraine|normandie|bretagne|provence|"
    r"saint|ville|fr)$",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
ACCENTED = re.compile(r"[éèêàçôûîâù]")
FRENCH_WORDS = {"le", "la", "les", "de", "des", "du", "et", "est", "une", "que", "qui", "pour",
                "dans", "avec", "pas", "par", "sur", "à", "en", "plus", "été", "être", "je"}

PLACE_VALUE = -0.8
ACCENT_VALUE = -0.1
DE_ET_VALUE = -0.15
POUR_A_VALUE = 0.2


def french_share(prefix, n=30):
    """Share of the last n tokens that are common French words."""
    words = [s.strip().lower() for s in prefix.token_strings[-n:]]
    return sum(w in FRENCH_WORDS for w in words) / len(words)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if FRENCH_PLACE.match(token):
        return carry, PLACE_VALUE
    if ACCENTED.search(token):
        return carry, ACCENT_VALUE
    if word in ("de", "et"):
        return carry, DE_ET_VALUE
    if word in ("pour", "à") and french_share(prefix) >= 0.1:
        return carry, POUR_A_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

    "aises", "ois", "oise", "oises", "ment", "tion", "tions", "ance",
    "ence", "é", "ée", "ées", "ité", "ités", "isme", "iste", "istes",
)

EDGE_PUNCTUATION = ".,:;!?()[]{}\"'’‘-–—"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc:
        _, previous, recent_french = carry

    piece = prefix.token_strings[-1]

            word = ""
    else:
        word = previous + piece
    word = word.strip(EDGE_PUNCTUATION)
    normalized = word.casefold()

    if normalized in FRANCOPHONE_TERMS:
        value = -0.60
    elif any(char in ACCENTS for char in normalized):
        value = -0.08
    elif normalized in FRENCH_FUNCTION_WORDS:
        value = -0.03
    elif word[:1].isupper() or any(recent_french):
        value = -0.10 if normalized.endswith(FRENCH_ENDINGS) else 0.0
    else:
        value = 0.0

    return (doc, word, recent_french), value

    """True if the text has a CJK, Hangul, Thai, Arabic, Cyrillic or accented Latin letter."""
    for ch in text:

            0x2E80 <= o <= 0x9FFF

the large values sit on the last letters of a word that is split across tokens. The strongest
case is a Cyrillic inflectional ending written as its own token: е or я (also ю, й, ё), as
in "делаете" -> "делает" + "е", "звенья" -> "звень" + "я", "объекте" -> "объект" + "е".
Latin-script word endings of the same kind, such as "e", "ye", "ya", "ev", "yer", "er"
(as in "walley" + "e", "Noy" + "e"), give a weaker signal.

The program is purely token-based: it predicts from the newest token only. It predicts
0.5 for a Cyrillic vowel-ending continuation piece, 0.15 for a Latin one, and 0 otherwise.
The values are scaled by least squares on training rows. Its variance explained is small,
because the real activation depends heavily on context and has large negative values on
code and identifier tokens that this program does not model.

# Latin-script endings of the same kind, weaker.

    """A word piece with no leading space that is made of letters only."""

                 + 0.24 * (not s.isascii())

resolve delete insert execute make register sort filter render run return
convert encode decode replace merge transform split join compare validate
apply generate prepare
""".split())

local global my your our selected short long all sub no num max min total
static public private auto async enabled valid invalid empty raw
""".split())
CONNECTORS = set('''
to from with on for by in and or as of into not after before
'''.split())

    word = word.lower()
    if word.endswith('s') and word[:-1] in DATA_WORDS:
        return word[:-1]
    return word

name type id key value count size path url uri info config context response
result version status index offset length len ref identifier metadata
""".split())

    word = root(word)
    if word in GET_OR_CREATE:

    if word in ACCESSORS:
        return 'other_call'
    if word in ACTIONS:
        return 'action'
    if word in MODIFIERS:
        return 'modifier'
    if word in CONNECTORS:
        return 'connector'
    if word in DATA_WORDS:
        return 'data'
    if len(word) <= 3:
        return 'short'
    return 'other'

    """Return naming style, suffix meaning, and preceding name-part meaning."""

    elif root(final) in DATA_WORDS:

    before = parts[-1] if parts else before

"""Layer-0 MLP feature for scientific vocabulary (down_proj component 1597).

What it does: this component writes a small signal that is large on the word being
completed in technical biomedical and physical-science writing, and negative on
clinical deficiency/inhibition/disease words. The program looks at the word that
ends at the current token (letters from the decoded text, so a word split over
several tokens such as "endoth|elial" is seen piece by piece) and returns:

        damage, injury, proliferation, ...) and for physical-property words
        (surface, area, volume, shape, stress, flow, pressure, fluid, ...)
  +0.2  for other technical nouns (section, region, distribution, material, ...)
  -0.35 for clinical words (deficiency, inhibitor, dependence, disorder, flu, ...)
  0     otherwise.
The values are the typical activation (in the component's units) for each class.
"""

CLINICAL = set("""deficiency deficient inhibitor inhibitors inhibition inhibited inhibits

def current_word(prefix):

    text = prefix.text_prefixes[-1]

"""Estimate context-sensitive responses to single capital Latin letters.

An alphabet table records letter preferences; A and I are weak. Capitalized
preceding words, academic titles, by/and/or, citation punctuation, and opening
brackets increase the estimate. Word interiors and uppercase runs weaken it.
Some punctuation-prefixed letter tokens are recognized too. A 100-character
text buffer resets at document boundaries; all other tokens receive -0.003.
The program omits diffuse activity and responses to other word fragments.
"""
import re

READS = ()
ACADEMIC_TITLES = {'Dr', 'Prof', 'Doctor', 'Professor'}
LETTER = {
    'A': -0.00,
    'B': 0.16,
    'C': 0.23,
    'D': 0.16,
    'E': 0.25,
    'F': 0.33,
    'G': 0.26,
    'H': 0.25,
    'I': -0.06,
    'J': 0.35,
    'K': 0.27,
    'L': 0.21,
    'M': 0.29,
    'N': 0.16,
    'O': 0.14,
    'P': 0.29,
    'Q': 0.05,
    'R': 0.21,
    'S': 0.22,
    'T': 0.21,
    'U': 0.15,
    'V': 0.12,
    'W': 0.29,
    'X': 0.05,
    'Y': 0.16,
    'Z': 0.11,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    start = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    tail = '' if start else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = token.strip()
    fused = re.fullmatch(r'[.\-:/_]\s*([A-Z])', text)
    letter = fused[1] if fused else text
    value = -0.003
    if letter in LETTER:
        last = tail.rstrip()[-1:] or ' '
        words = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+', tail)
        word = words[-1] if words else ''
        boundary = (not tail or tail[-1].isspace() or
                    token[0].isspace() or not last.isalnum())
        value = LETTER[letter]
        if last.islower():
            value -= 0.05 if boundary else 0.17
        elif last.isupper():
            value -= 0.08 if boundary else 0.18
        elif last in '.,;':
            value += 0.15
        elif last in '([':
            value += 0.14
        elif last in '{_=+*\\$\"\'`':
            value -= 0.06
        if word.istitle() and len(word) > 1:
            value += 0.09 if last.isalnum() else 0.14
        elif len(word) == 1 and word.isupper() and not last.isalnum():
            value += 0.07
        if boundary and word in ACADEMIC_TITLES:
            value += 0.18
        if boundary and word.lower() == 'by':
            value += 0.23
        if boundary and word.lower() in {'and', 'or'}:
            value += 0.16
        if re.search(r'\n\s*$', tail):
            value += 0.07
        if re.search(r'\d[.;]\s*$', tail):
            value += 0.10
        if not boundary and not fused and last.isupper():
            value = -0.026
        if start:
            value -= 0.16
    return (doc, (tail + token)[-100:]), float(value)

UP_AFTER = {"take", "took", "taken", "taking", "takes", "make", "made", "makes",

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    before = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    if any(ch in token for ch in OCCUPY_CHINESE):
